sites.meaning: Branch to an ownership guard; retain the original transfer implementation and all read/RMW wrappers.

Executable padding holds spmi-owner-guard.S. Bound the relative APID, permit observer reads, reject writes when the cached node owner differs from the caller EE, then execute the original prologue. Errors report zero transferred bytes.
Start the transaction without a pre-command STATUS read, following Linux ordering. Original WDATA/CMD writes and bounded post-command STATUS polling remain intact.

evidence.reference: Working supplied Y703 image has all 24576 SPMI .text bytes identical to TB520FU stock; it does not stub transfer functions.
evidence.live_TWRP: Arbiter version 0x70010000, features0 0x80060380, features1 0x80; bus0=896, bus1=128. APID 0x4c PPID 0x183 owner=4, APID 0x277 PPID 0x021 owner=0, AP EE=0.
evidence.fault: Earlier fault at SPMI+0x37f0 on write STATUS 0x0c54c008 matches the unowned 0x4c channel. The earlier 0x277 fault was on an owned channel; command-first ordering is a hypothesis requiring a tablet boot test, not a proven firewall fix.

limitations: Hardware untested. Ownership is necessary but may not be sufficient for MMIO access after ABL. An owned-channel fault can still occur. Reads, writes, data buffers and failure status now remain real; no successful no-op transfers. PMIC cold-init remains deferred.
